claims.statement: Delegated design: semantic workspace-query is a front door over the existing build and query functions, not a new operation. It resolves the checkout root, a commit (--ref, default HEAD) and a repository label, builds or reuses a derived SQLite index of that committed revision at <index-dir>/<clone-key>/<sha>.sqlite in a per-user cache outside every checkout, and returns the knowledge-query payload plus an additive workspace_index object. Only committed bytes are indexed: the active checkout when it is clean at that commit, otherwise a temporary worktree. knowledge-query stays read-only with explicit identity arguments; changes and history are refused because one cache file holds one commit.

attributes.scope: Agent-selected design within the owner's construction delegation under ADR 0031; not an owner-ratified cache, identity or distribution policy.
attributes.decision_changed: Whether an agent with no prepared index can ask what reviewed records say about a file in one command, and what a later change to the cache location, label derivation, retention or cache trust must preserve.
attributes.safety_basis: The derived label uses only the last two path segments of the origin URL and is dropped when a kept segment contains @ or :, so the URL's credentials and host are not printed. The clone-key directory and the database path are refused when either is a symlink or resolves elsewhere, which covers a Windows junction. An index directory inside the checkout is refused.
attributes.known_limits: A reused cache file is trusted as written and is not re-verified against Git; anyone who can write to the index directory can alter answers. At most 8 snapshot files are kept per clone, pruned by modification time after a build. Uncommitted changes to the indexer itself are not detected; --refresh rebuilds. The label is unverified. The first call for a commit pays a build: about 20 s through a temporary worktree and 2 to 5 s on reuse on the development host.
attributes.claim_ceiling: Exercised through the real CLI on one Windows host at baaec6b9 with the change uncommitted: payload equality with the two-step path for seven operations, and scratch-repository probes of labels, refs, retention, a junction and unreadable cache files. Symlink refusal NOT_RUN (no privilege on the host); POSIX locations and modes NOT_RUN; unit tests NOT_RUN. Whether agents consult reviewed records earlier because of it is NOT TESTED.

claims.statement: Rejected alternative: make --db, --repository and --target-ref optional on knowledge-query and resolve them from --repo. knowledge-query is documented and used as a read-only operation over an explicitly identified index; resolving them implicitly would add a cache write and a temporary worktree to it, and a partly explicit argument matrix to validate. A separate command keeps that contract and confines the new side effects to one name.

attributes.scope: Engineering alternative for where zero-setup index resolution lives.

claims.statement: Deferred alternative: build the snapshot from Git objects without any checkout, which would remove the temporary-worktree cost of a dirty tree (roughly 10 s of a 15 to 20 s first call on the development host). The builder reads and fingerprints files from a checkout, and its tracked-file, symlink and filter checks assume one; object bytes can differ from checkout bytes under line-ending conversion, so the two build routes could give different fingerprints for one commit.

attributes.scope: Engineering alternative for how a commit is materialized for indexing; the fingerprint difference is inferred from the source and was not run.
attributes.revisit_when: First-call latency is shown to keep agents from querying, or snapshots must be byte-identical across platforms.

At deb19d05, the explicit installer maps a host and scope chosen by the caller to a filesystem discovery root and copies packaged Skill trees there. A destination is missing, current or different by tree fingerprint; against the root's install record (.sensemaking-skills-install.json) a different copy is outdated, changed or unrecorded, and from a Git checkout an unrecorded copy equal to a committed version of skills/<name> is historical. Only --update (outdated or historical) or --force replaces a different copy. It never detects the active host and does not establish what a host loaded.

attributes.revision_history: REVISED 2026-11-10 (PR #798): the db821c25 statement named only missing/current/different; install-record classification and --update were added. claims.statement: Delegated design at deb19d05: when setup-skills runs from a Git checkout, a divergent copy with no install record is compared with every version of skills/<name> committed on the checkout's branches, tags, remote-tracking refs and HEAD. A copy whose Git tree id equals one of them, computed locally with every file as mode 100644, byte for byte or after CRLF to LF in files without NUL bytes, is historical: its content is recoverable from Git, so --update replaces it and the report names the commit. Other unrecorded copies, symlinked or junctioned copies and trees containing links still need --force. Matching never writes the install record; a replaced copy is recorded as replaced.

attributes.scope: Agent-selected design within the owner's construction delegation; extends decision:install-record-classifies-divergent-skill-copies without changing what the record means. Not an owner-ratified distribution policy.
attributes.decision_changed: Whether a Skill root installed before install records existed can be updated without --force replacing every divergent copy, and which evidence makes an unrecorded copy safe to replace.
attributes.safety_basis: Replacing a historical copy loses nothing that is not in a commit reachable from a ref at the time of the run. CRLF-only equality follows the line_ending_only drift class scripts/repo_probes.py already uses.
attributes.known_limits: Only a source checkout whose top level is the parent of the skills directory; wheel installs have no history and keep the old behavior. A copy written from an uncommitted working tree, or from a commit no longer reachable from any ref, stays unrecorded. A committed file stored with mode 100755 cannot match. About 0.5 s per unrecorded copy on this host (two Git subprocesses).
attributes.claim_ceiling: Exercised through the real CLI on scratch copies of one Windows host's ~/.claude/skills at deb19d05: 23 of 24 unrecorded copies matched (13 byte for byte, 10 apart from CRLF), one with a nested duplicate directory and one hand-edited copy were refused and preserved byte for byte. Unit tests NOT_RUN.

The record would then vouch for trees setup-skills neither wrote nor verified against its source, which the record's meaning excludes; classifying at run time uses the same evidence without persisting a claim.

Unrecorded copies needed --force under this decision alone; since PR #799, --update also replaces one that decision:committed-history-identifies-unrecorded-skill-copies classifies as historical.
